item.title: ASCO 2026 - Multiple Myeloma
item.description:
• Summary: At ASCO 2026, Bristol Myers Squibb presented positive Phase 3 data for mezigdomide, a next-generation CELMoD agent designed as a successor to Pomalyst (pomalidomide) in multiple myeloma. Simultaneously, Johnson & Johnson showcased a comprehensive portfolio covering multiple myeloma with its approved and investigational agents, including Darzalex (daratumumab) and Kyprolis (carfilzomib). These presentations highlight the ongoing competition and innovation in the multiple myeloma treatment landscape.
  • MoAs: Mezigdomide: Cereblon E3 ligase modulator (CELMoD) that degrades Ikaros and Aiolos transcription factors, leading to anti-myeloma effects. Pomalidomide: Immunomodulatory drug (IMiD) that binds cereblon, also degrades Ikaros/Aiolos.
  • Sources: STAT News, BioPharma Dive, ApexOnco, Endpoints News

item.title: ASCO 2026 - Lung Cancer
item.description:
• Summary: At ASCO 2026, Merck & Co. presented data for its TROP2-directed antibody-drug conjugate sacituzumab tirumotecan (sac-TMT) in non-small cell lung cancer. Additionally, AstraZeneca reported positive results in bladder cancer, outperforming Pfizer in a head-to-head trial.
  • MoAs: Sacituzumab tirumotecan: Humanized anti-TROP2 monoclonal antibody conjugated to a topoisomerase I inhibitor payload, delivering cytotoxic drug to TROP2-expressing tumor cells.
  • Sources: BioPharma Dive, ApexOnco

item.title: Replimune Melanoma Drug
item.description:
• Summary: Replimune announced it will resubmit its lead oncolytic immunotherapy, RP1, for FDA approval in melanoma after previous rejections. The company is encouraged by changes in FDA leadership and hopes to address earlier concerns. RP1 is a genetically modified herpes simplex virus type 1 designed to infect and lyse tumor cells while stimulating a systemic immune response.
  • MoAs: RP1: Oncolytic herpes simplex virus type 1 engineered to express GM-CSF and a fusogenic glycoprotein (GALV-GP R-), promoting tumor cell lysis, antigen release, and dendritic cell activation to boost anti-tumor immunity.
  • Sources: BioPharma Dive, Endpoints News, BioSpace

item.title: Agios Tebapivat Failure
item.description:
• Summary: Agios Pharmaceuticals discontinued development of tebapivat (AG-946) in low-risk myelodysplastic syndromes (MDS) after a Phase 3 trial failed to meet its primary endpoint. The drug, a pyruvate kinase R activator, was being investigated for anemia in MDS. Agios will continue to evaluate tebapivat in sickle cell disease, where it still holds promise.
  • MoAs: Tebapivat: Small-molecule activator of pyruvate kinase R (PKR), increasing ATP production and reducing hemolysis in red blood cells, thereby improving anemia.
  • Sources: Endpoints News, Fierce Biotech

item.title: AstraZeneca Imfinzi Label Expansion
item.description:
• Summary: AstraZeneca is pursuing a label expansion for Imfinzi (durvalumab) and its combination with tremelimumab following a failed trial outcome, seeking to broaden its use in oncology.
  • MoAs: PD-L1 inhibitor, CTLA-4 inhibitor
  • Sources: Endpoints News

item.title: Summit PD-1/VEGF at ASCO
item.description:
• Summary: Summit's PD-1/VEGF bispecific antibody (ivonescimab) is set to take center stage at ASCO, potentially reshaping the competitive landscape for PD-1 therapies.
  • MoAs: PD-1 checkpoint inhibitor, VEGF inhibitor (bispecific antibody)
  • Sources: BioSpace

item.title: Dizal Survival Benefit at ASCO
item.description:
• Summary: Dizal's survival benefit data for sunvozertinib presented at ASCO 2026 may be confounded by crossover in the trial design, complicating interpretation of overall survival.
  • MoAs: EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor (irreversible, targeting exon20 insertion mutations)
  • Sources: ApexOnco

item.title: Legend Scientific CAR-T
item.description:
• Summary: Legend Scientific's founder returns to ASCO with a new ambition for high-yield, non-gene-edited CAR-T therapies, highlighting innovative approaches to cell therapy manufacturing.
  • MoAs: Chimeric antigen receptor T-cell therapy
  • Sources: Fierce Biotech
